sections.title: 英语知识运用
sections.directions: Directions: Read the following text. Choose the best word(s) for each numbered blank and mark A, B, C or D on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)

questions.analysis: prepared 【线索】前句说'此话题没人敢说' 上一句强调这个观点 is one of those hypotheses that dare not speak its name，接着用 【选项】A) selected ✗ 语义被动、与文意不符 B) prepared ✓ be prepared to=愿意/做好准备 prepared 与 to say 搭配为 be prepared to do='愿意/做好准备去做'，紧承 But 的转折语气 ——别人不敢说，他却愿意/做好准备去说，与 dare not speak its name. But 一脉相承。 C) obliged ✗ 义为'被迫'，色彩相反 D) pleased ✗ 情绪'高兴'过重，文意没有 pleased 指'乐于/高兴'，话题敏感、'might tremble'后文也暗示压力，不会是单纯的'高兴去说'， 【验证】代回原句：But Gregory Cochran is __(1)__ to say it anyway 即 he is prepared to say it 家这条 outline 完全一致。

rare 【线索】同位语解释'罕见'之处 空后的同位语 a scientist who works independently __(3)__ any institution 给出原因 【选项】A) unique ✗ 程度过强、不搭 bird unique 意为'独一无二'，程度极强，而后文同位语只说他 works independently __(3)__ any institution，不是世上唯一一人，且 a unique bird 不是英语习惯说法。 B) particular ✗ 义为'特定/挑剔'，不指罕见 particular 多表示'特指的某个'或'挑剔'，并不传达'稀有'，且 a particular bird 不是固定隐喻。 C) special ✗ 泛指'特别'，搭配不地道 special 笼统、无'稀有'之意，且与 bird 连用无固定隐喻意义。 D) rare ✓ rare bird=罕见之人 rare 与 bird 组成英语习语 a rare bird，专指'罕见的人/异类'，正好被同位语 a scientist who works independently __(3)__ any institution（独立于任何机构的科学家）所佐证，是同义并行 【验证】代回：he is that rare bird, a scientist who works independently of any institution

of 【线索】independent(ly) of 固定搭配 空所在结构 a scientist who works independently __(3)__ any institution 中， independently 的固定搭配为 independent(ly) of='独立于…之外'，无需跨句寻找。 【选项】 A) of ✓ independently of 是固定搭配 of 与 independently 构成 be/work independently of='独立于…之外'，意为他不依附 any institution，与上文 rare bird 的孤胆形象一致。 B) with ✗ 搭配不存在 with 表'与…一起'，与 independently'独立地'语义冲突，且没有 independently with 的固定 C) in ✗ 搭配不存在 in 与 independently 不构成固定搭配，be independent in 之类用法多接抽象品质，不接机构。 D) against ✗ 语义过激、无搭配 【验证】代回：works independently of any institution='独立于任何机构之外工作'，与 rare bird

previously 【线索】原以为非细菌→实际却是感染 原文 some diseases not __(4)__ thought to have a bacterial cause were actually infections 是一种'过去认为…而实际…'的对照——'were actually infections'是被推翻的真 【选项】A) subsequently ✗ 义为'随后'，时间方向反 subsequently='后来、随后'，但句意要的是'此前曾被认为'，方向相反。 B) presently ✗ '当前/不久'，与对照不符 C) previously ✓ '此前'与 actually 形成对照 previously='以前'，与后文 were actually infections 形成'previously thought… actually were…'的经典对照，正是 Cochran 所推翻的旧观念。 D) lately ✗ '最近'，与对照不符 lately='最近'，意味着新近的看法，与'被 Cochran 推翻的旧看法'冲突。 【验证】代回：some diseases not previously thought to have a bacterial cause were actually

Even 【线索】前一段塑造他'敢说'，本句却说他'会发抖' 前文 But Gregory Cochran is __(1)__ to say it anyway 强调他敢说；本句 he, however, might tremble at the __(6)__ of what he is about to do 却说他可能也会发抖。前后是'即 【选项】A) Only ✗ '只有他'与上下文矛盾 B) So ✗ 顺承因果，与 however 冲突 C) Even ✓ '连他都…'让步强调 Even he='连他这样敢说的人也…'，与后面 however, might tremble 共同构成让步语气：连这 D) Hence ✗ 因果，与 however 冲突 Hence='因此'，因果方向，与紧随其后的 however 互斥。 【验证】代回：Even he, however, might tremble at the thought of what he is about to do that one group of humanity is more intelligent than the others, but explains the

thought 【线索】后接 of 引导的从句内容 空后是 of what he is about to do——'他即将要做的事'，这是一种抽象的预想，而非可看 见的实物，所以最契合的是 at the thought of='一想到…就…'这个固定搭配。 【选项】 A) thought ✓ at the thought of=一想到 thought 与 at the…of 构成 at the thought of='一想到…'，并与 tremble 高度匹配，意为'一想 到自己将做的事，他都会发抖'，与 Even he, however, might tremble 的让步基调完全一致。 B) sight ✗ 需接可见之物 sight 用于 at the sight of 后接具体可见对象（血、危险场景等），但 what he is about to do 是 C) cost ✗ 搭配偏'代价'，文意未涉及 cost 常与 at the cost of='以…为代价'连用，意思偏物质/牺牲，与 tremble 也不直接搭配，文意 D) risk ✗ 搭配偏'冒…风险'，方向偏 risk 多用于 at the risk of='冒…的危险'，强调'冒险去做'，而本句强调的是'仅仅想一想就会发抖'的 【验证】代回：might tremble at the thought of what he is about to do——'一想到自己将做的

suggests 【线索】not only…but explains 并列结构 原文为 a paper which not only __(7)__ that one group of humanity is more intelligent than the others, but explains the process，并列谓语是 explains（解释过程），空里要 【选项】A) advises ✗ '建议'，主体不对 B) suggests ✓ suggest that=表明/暗示主张 C) protests ✗ '抗议'，情绪色彩相反 D) objects ✗ '反对'，方向相反 objects 表'反对'，object to/that 也带否定立场，但论文是在论证一个肯定命题，方向反。 【验证】代回：a paper which not only suggests that one group of humanity is more intelligent than the others, but explains the process——'这篇论文不仅提出某一族群比

question 【线索】对前句论文主张中那个'人群'的回指 上句 one group of humanity is more intelligent than the others 引出了一个群体，下句 The group in __(8)__ is a particular people originated from central Europe 显然是回 【选项】A) progress ✗ '进行中'，与人群不搭 progress in progress='进行中'，多用于事件/工程，不修饰人群。 B) fact ✗ in fact 不修饰名词 fact in fact='事实上'是句子状语，不能作 The group 的定语短语。 C) need ✗ '需要帮助的'，文意没有 D) question ✓ in question=所讨论的 question in question='所讨论的、提及的'，正好回指上句 one group of humanity，是该群体 【验证】代回：The group in question is a particular people originated from central Europe

scoring 【线索】IQ 测试与高于平均 12-15 分 原文 does well in IQ test, __(9)__ 12-15 points above the __(10)__ value of 100——在 IQ 测试中表现好，'得分'高于平均 12-15 分，宾语是 12-15 points（分数），最自然的搭 配是 score points='得分多少分'。 【选项】A) attaining ✗ 通常接目标，不接分差 attaining 常与 goal/level/age 搭配，如 attain a high level；用'达到 12-15 分高于平均'不地 道，因为 12-15 points above 是分差而非绝对水平。 B) scoring ✓ score points 固定搭配 scoring 与 points 搭配是英语考试/比赛语境下'得分'的固定说法，scoring 12-15 points above the mean='得分高于平均值 12-15 分'，与 IQ test 的语境完美契合。 C) reaching ✗ 接绝对值不接分差 reaching 可接绝对数值（reaching 115），但这里是'high above the mean'的相对差距，不是直 D) calculating ✗ '计算'，主体不对 【验证】代回：generally does well in IQ test, scoring 12-15 points above the mean value of 100——'该群体在 IQ 测试中表现良好，得分高于平均值 100 的 12-15 分'，自然顺畅，并 与 outline 第三段'高 IQ 现象'对接。

mean 【线索】12-15 points above the ___ value of 100 原文 scoring 12-15 points above the __(10)__ value of 100——12-15 分'高于…的 100 【选项】A) normal ✗ '正常的'，含'非异常'判断 normal value 可表'正常值'，但隐含'非异常'判断，IQ=100 在统计上是均值而非'正常区间'，且 normal value 不是 IQ 测试通用术语。 B) common ✗ '常见的'，非统计术语 common value='常见值'，类似于众数概念，但 IQ=100 是均值，不是'最常见的值'。 C) mean ✓ mean value=均值 mean 在统计学中作形容词意为'平均的'，mean value=均值，正好与 IQ 测验设定均值为 100 这一常识一致；且与前文 scoring 12-15 points above'高于均值 12-15 分'完美搭配。 D) total ✗ '总值'，逻辑荒谬 total value='总值'，IQ 不是累加值，不存在'总分 100'，且'高于总分 12-15 分'更说不通。 【验证】代回：above the mean value of 100——'高于均值 100'，与统计常识（IQ 标准化为均值

disproportionately 【线索】高 IQ 群体在西方知识与文化中的贡献 原文 has contributed __(11)__ to the intellectual and cultural life of the West, as the __(12)__ of their elites, including several world-renowned scientists, __(13)__——该群 【选项】A) unconsciously ✗ '无意识地'，方向不对 B) disproportionately ✓ '不成比例地（多）' disproportionately='不成比例地'，常用于表达'贡献相对于人口比例之大'，与下文 including several world-renowned scientists 这类佐证完美对应——人口少但精英多。 C) indefinitely ✗ '无限期地'，时间维度，文意不符 D) unaccountably ✗ '莫名其妙地'，文章后给出原因 unaccountably='无法解释地'，但文章后半部分恰恰给出了 unique evolutionary pressures 这一 【验证】代回：has contributed disproportionately to the intellectual and cultural life of the world-renowned scientists 印证，逻辑通畅且与全局立场一致。

careers 【线索】其精英'怎么了'+包含若干世界知名科学家 原文 as the __(12)__ of their elites, including several world-renowned scientists, __(13)__——后接 including several world-renowned scientists 说明精英们以'世界知名 【选项】A) missions ✗ '使命'，与'印证贡献'不直接 B) fortunes ✗ '财富/命运'，与智识贡献不对应 C) interests ✗ '兴趣/利益'，过于个人 D) careers ✓ careers of elites=精英的事业 careers 与 elites 搭配指'精英的职业生涯/事业'，正好由 including several world-renowned 【验证】代回：as the careers of their elites, including several world-renowned scientists,

affirm 【线索】as the careers of their elites…___ 主语 careers 原文 as the __(12)__ of their elites, including several world-renowned scientists, __(13)__ 中，空 13 的主语是 the careers of their elites，as 引导'正如…所证实/所表明 【选项】 A) affirm ✓ affirm=证实，主语可为无生命证据 B) witness ✗ '见证'，主语多为时间地点 witness='见证'时，主语典型是 the 20th century / Beijing 等时代地点；让 careers 'witness'不 C) observe ✗ '观察/遵守'，无证实之义 observe 主语多为人，意为'观察、遵守'，不能由 careers 做主语'观察'某事。 D) approve ✗ '批准/认可'，主语应为人 【验证】代回：as the careers of their elites, including several world-renowned scientists,

however 【线索】前两句并列了 IQ 高与遗传病多，下句却说'以前没人把它俩联系起来' 前文一句 does well in IQ test，另一句 They also suffer more often than most people from a number of nasty genetic diseases, such as breast cancer 列出两组事实；空所 在句 These facts, __(14)__, have previously been thought unrelated 出现'These facts'回指，'have previously been thought unrelated'是与前文的'反差'——本应有联系 【选项】A) moreover ✗ 递进，与转折语气冲突 B) therefore ✗ 因果，与文意无关 C) however ✓ 转折，引出'此前被认为无关' however='然而'，与下文 have previously been thought unrelated 一起表明：尽管两组事实 D) meanwhile ✗ 时间并列，无反差感 【验证】代回：These facts, however, have previously been thought unrelated——'然而这些事

put down 【线索】前者被归因于社会因素 原文 The former has been __(15)__ to social effects, such as a strong tradition of __(16)__ education——The former 指'高 IQ'这件事，过去一直被'归因于'社会因素（如重 【选项】A) given up ✗ '放弃'，意思相反 B) got over ✗ '克服'，宾语应是困难 C) carried on ✗ '继续'，与 to 搭配生硬 carried on='继续做'，不与 to 引导原因连用，搭配不通。 D) put down ✓ put down to=归因于 put down 与 to 搭配为 put X down to Y='把 X 归因于 Y'，意为'高 IQ 此前被归因于社会因 素，如重视教育的传统'，与下文 such as a strong tradition of __(16)__ education 列举的'原 【验证】代回：The former has been put down to social effects, such as a strong tradition of 句 The latter was seen as a (an) __(17)__ of genetic isolation 形成'前者归因…后者归

valuing 【线索】用以解释'为何 IQ 高'的社会传统 原文 The former has been put down to social effects, such as a strong tradition of __(16)__ education——既然要解释高 IQ，那么这种'传统'应是促进/重视教育的传统；'重 【选项】A) assessing ✗ '评估'，与传统语义不搭 assessing education='评估教育'是行政行为，不是一种解释族群高 IQ 的文化传统。 B) supervising ✗ '监督'，行为偏制度 supervising education='监督教育'是管理动作，与'文化传统重视'相去甚远。 C) administering ✗ '管理/施行'，无'重视'之义 administering education='管理/施行教育'是行政性动作，与'群体性传统重视教育'语义脱节。 D) valuing ✓ valuing education=重视教育 valuing education='重视教育'，是该族群常被提到的文化传统，恰好可作'高 IQ'的社会解释， 与上文 put down to social effects 的归因链对应。 【验证】代回：a strong tradition of valuing education——'一种深厚的重视教育的传统'，紧扣高

consequence 【线索】后者（遗传病）被视为基因隔离的结果 原文 The latter was seen as a (an) __(17)__ of genetic isolation——The latter 指'遗传 【选项】A) development ✗ '发展'，与'病'不搭 development of='…的发展'，遗传病不是'基因隔离的发展'，逻辑不顺。 B) origin ✗ 因果方向反 C) consequence ✓ consequence of=…的结果 与 14 题 however、15 题 put down to 形成'旧解释体系'：高 IQ 归因社会，遗传病归因基因 D) instrument ✗ '工具'，逻辑荒谬 instrument of='…的工具'，遗传病不是基因隔离的工具，逻辑不通。 【验证】代回：The latter was seen as a consequence of genetic isolation——'后者被视为基因 隔离的结果'，与前一句 The former has been put down to social effects 形成两种独立

linked 【线索】Cochran 提出二者'密切相关' 原文 Dr. Cochran suggests that the intelligence and diseases are intimately __(18)__ ——Cochran 主张'智力和疾病紧密相连'，下一句 His argument is that the unusual history of these people has __(19)__ them to unique evolutionary pressures that have resulted in this __(20)__ state of affairs 进一步说明二者来源相同。'相联'是因果/统 【选项】 A) linked ✓ be intimately linked=密切关联 linked 与 intimately 形成 intimately linked='密切相连'，是科研论文中表'有内在联系'的标准搭 B) integrated ✗ '整合为整体'，过于强 C) woven ✗ '编织'，比喻不当 D) combined ✗ '结合'，偏物理层面 【验证】代回：the intelligence and diseases are intimately linked——'智力与疾病紧密相连'， 正是 Cochran 这篇大胆论文的核心论断，呼应 outline 中'第三段末由 Cochran 提出 unique evolutionary pressures 这一统一解释'。

subjected 【线索】非凡历史使他们遭受独特进化压力 原文 the unusual history of these people has __(19)__ them to unique evolutionary 力，最契合 subject to。 【选项】A) limited ✗ '限于'，文意不符 B) subjected ✓ subject sb. to=使遭受 subjected them to unique evolutionary pressures='使他们遭受独特的进化压力'，精确对 应'独特历史→独特进化压力'的因果链，并为下一句 resulted in this __(20)__ state of affairs 做 C) converted ✗ '转变为'，对象不对 converted them to='把他们转变为'，多接结果状态（信仰/物质），把人转变为'进化压力'语义 D) directed ✗ '指向'，与压力不搭 directed them to='把他们引向…'，强调方向引导，但进化压力是'施加'而非'引导前往'，搭配 【验证】代回：the unusual history of these people has subjected them to unique evolutionary pressures——'他们的非凡历史使他们遭受了独特的进化压力'，与 outline 并存）。

paradoxical 【线索】智力与疾病同源、看似矛盾 全段从 They also suffer more often than most people from a number of nasty genetic diseases 摆出'高 IQ 与高发遗传病并存'的反差现象，到 the intelligence and diseases are intimately __(18)__ 揭示二者同源；这种'高智力与遗传病同时存在且彼此关 联'的局面正是英语中的 paradox。 【选项】 A) paradoxical ✓ paradoxical=看似矛盾的 paradoxical state of affairs='看似矛盾的局面'，紧扣全段反差——智力高（好）与遗传病多 章开篇 dare not speak its name 那种'反常识'的张力。 B) incompatible ✗ '不相容'，但事实是并存 们关联到同一原因，与 incompatible 的'不可共存'矛盾。 C) inevitable ✗ '不可避免'，并非论点重点 D) continuous ✗ '持续的'，文意没有 【验证】代回：have resulted in this paradoxical state of affairs——'造成了如今这种看似矛盾 OVERVIEW · 通读建境 全文围绕 Gregory Cochran 的一项颇具争议的研究：他主张 one group of humanity is more intelligent than the others，并将这种高智商与该群体高发的遗传病视为同一自然选 择过程的产物，最终在末段明确 the intelligence and diseases are intimately __(18)__。作 者基调是客观转述，多次用 aroused much controversy、might tremble at 等词暗示话题敏 第一段是人物背景铺垫：Cochran 是独立学者，敢说别人不敢说的话——dare not speak its name、He helped popularize the idea that some diseases not __(4)__ thought to have a bacterial cause were actually infections。第二段亮论文核心命题：one group of humanity is more intelligent than the others 且解释机制为 natural selection。第三段先并列两组事实 ——高 IQ 与 nasty genetic diseases, such as breast cancer——再用 __(14)__ 转折出旧解释 （社会因素 / 基因隔离）的不足，最后由 Cochran 提出 unique evolutionary pressures 这 SENTENCE INSIGHTS · 句子精讲 2 But Gregory Cochran is prepared to say it anyway. sections.title: 阅读理解
sections.directions: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions after each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)

blocks.content: While still catching up to men in some spheres of modern life, women appear to be way ahead in at least one undesirable category. "Women are particularly susceptible to developing depression and anxiety disorders in response to stress compared to men," according to Dr. Yehuda, chief psychiatrist at New York's Veteran's Administration Hospital. Studies of both animals and humans have shown that sex hormones somehow affect the stress response, causing females under stress to produce more of the trigger chemicals than do males under the same conditions. In several of the studies, when stressed-out female rats had their ovaries (the female reproductive organs) removed, their chemical responses became equal to those of the males. Adding to a woman's increased dose of stress chemicals, are her increased "opportunities" for stress. "It's not necessarily that women don't cope as well. It's just that they have so much more to cope with," says Dr. Yehuda. "Their capacity for tolerating stress may even be greater than men's," she observes, "it's just that they're dealing with so many more things that they become worn out from it more visibly and sooner." In 1784, five years before he became president of the United States, George Washington, 52, was nearly toothless. So he hired a dentist to transplant nine teeth into his jaw – having extracted them from the mouths of his slaves. That's a far different image from the cherry-tree-chopping George most people remember from their history books. But recently, many historians have begun to focus on the role slavery played in the lives of the founding generation. They have been spurred in part by DNA evidence made available in 1998, which almost certainly proved Thomas Jefferson had fathered at least one child with his slave Sally Hemings. And only over the past 30 years have scholars examined history from the bottom up. Works of several historians reveal the moral compromises made by the nation's early leaders and the fragile nature of the country's infancy. More significantly, they argue that many of the Founding Fathers knew slavery was wrong – and yet most did little to fight it. More than anything, the historians say, the founders were hampered by the culture of their time. While Washington and Jefferson privately expressed distaste for slavery, they also understood that it was part of the political and economic bedrock of the country they helped to create. For one thing, the South could not afford to part with its slaves. Owning slaves was "like having a large bank account," says Wiencek, author of An Imperfect God: George Washington, His Slaves, and the Creation of America. The southern states would not have signed the Constitution without protections for the "peculiar institution," including a clause that counted a slave as three fifths of a man for purposes of congressional representation. And the statesmen's political lives depended on slavery. The three-fifths formula handed Jefferson his narrow victory in the presidential election of 1800 by inflating the votes of the southern states in the Electoral College. Once in office, Jefferson extended slavery with the Louisiana Purchase in 1803; the new land was carved into 13 states, including three slave states. Still, Jefferson freed Hemings's children – though not Hemings herself or his approximately 150 other slaves. Washington, who had begun to believe that all men were created equal after observing the bravery of the black soldiers during the Revolutionary War, overcame the strong opposition of his relatives to grant his slaves their freedom in his will. blocks.content: In his autobiography, Darwin himself speaks of his intellectual powers with extraordinary modesty. He points out that he always experienced much difficulty in expressing himself clearly and concisely, but (46)he believes that this very difficulty may have had the compensating advantage of forcing him to think long and intently about every sentence, and thus enabling him to detect errors in reasoning and in his own observations. He disclaimed the possession of any great quickness of apprehension or wit, such as distinguished Huxley. (47)He asserted, also, that his power to follow a long and purely abstract train of thought was very limited, for which reason he felt certain that he never could have succeeded with mathematics. His memory, too, he described as extensive, but hazy. So poor in one sense was it that he never could remember for more than a few days a single date or a line of poetry. (48)On the other hand, he did not accept as well founded the charge made by some of his critics that, while he was a good observer, he had no power of reasoning. This, he thought, could not be true, because the "Origin of Species" is one long argument from the beginning to the end, and has convinced many able men. No one, he submits, could have written it without possessing some power of reasoning. He was willing to assert that "I have a fair share of invention, and of common sense or judgment, such as every fairly successful lawyer or doctor must have, but not, I believe, in any higher degree." (49)He adds humbly that perhaps he was "superior to the common run of men in noticing things which easily escape attention, and in observing them carefully." Writing in the last year of his life, he expressed the opinion that in two or three respects his mind had changed during the preceding twenty or thirty years. Up to the age of thirty or beyond it poetry of many kinds gave him great pleasure. Formerly, too, pictures had given him considerable, and music very great, delight. In 1881, however, he said: "Now for many years I cannot endure to read a line of poetry. I have also almost lost my taste for pictures or music." (50)Darwin was convinced that the loss of these tastes was not only a loss of happiness, but might possibly be injurious to the intellect, and more probably to the moral character.
